content.title: About
content.content: Pie pumpkin is a variety of pumpkin with smooth orange flesh that is usually peeled, seeded and eaten raw in salads, smoothies or as an ingredient for baking. It has a mild sweet flavor and a tender texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pie pumpkin belongs to the Cucurbitaceae family and is a close relative of zucchini and other pumpkins.
The name comes from its frequent use in American pumpkin pies and desserts.
It contains higher levels of beta‑carotene than most other pumpkin varieties, giving it a bright orange color.
When stored in an airtight container, it can keep in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks.
In the United States it is a traditional ingredient for Thanksgiving pumpkin pie.

items.title: Rich in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene is converted to vitamin A in the body, supporting vision, immunity and skin health.

items.title: Low‑calorie source of fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C provides antioxidant protection and enhances iron absorption.

items.title: Good source of potassium
items.content: Potassium supports normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Provides folate
items.content: Folate is essential for DNA synthesis and is especially important during pregnancy.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to pumpkin, resulting in skin rash or swelling.

items.title: Food spoilage
items.content: If stored too long or under improper conditions, mold can develop, leading to foodborne illness.

items.title: High natural sugar
items.content: Raw pumpkin pieces contain natural sugars, which should be considered by people with diabetes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the pumpkin thinly for salads, blend it into smoothies, use it in raw baking recipes, or stuff it into other vegetables. It is typically peeled and seeded before consumption.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep peeled pumpkin in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C. For longer storage, freeze the pieces in a freezer‑safe bag.
